svg.title: How a USPS PO Box works, as USPS.com and the Domestic Mail Manual describe it: choose a Post Office, size and term; apply online or in person on PS Form 1093; show two forms of ID at the counter and get two keys or the combination; pay by the 10th of the month the payment is due; packages that do not fit go to a counter slip or a parcel locker.
svg.text: USPS PO Box
Per USPS.com, a USPS FAQ and the DMM
1. Choose
A Post Office, a box size (five sizes)
and a term. Prices differ by location.
2. Apply
Online or at a Post Office,
on PS Form 1093.
3. Show ID at the counter
2 forms of ID (the DMM: one primary,
one secondary). Online: within 30 days.
Then you get 2 keys or the combination.
4. Keep it up
Pay for a full term in advance. USPS.com:
pay by the 10th of the month the payment
is due; if unpaid, the box closes on the
11th of that month.
Where the pages differ
Late payment: a USPS FAQ says service
ends if payment is not received by the
10th day after the due date. Terms: 3, 6 or
12 months (USPS.com, FAQ) against 3, 6 or
two 6-month periods (DMM). Ask the Post
Office where the box is which applies.
Closing and refunds
A refund may be possible. It depends on
the term and how long you had the box.
Packages that do not fit
USPS.com: a slip for the counter,
or a secure parcel locker.
Sources: USPS.com, Rent a PO Box; USPS FAQ,
PO Box - The Basics (Oct. 16, 2026); Domestic Mail
Manual 508, section 4.0 (read Nov. 6, 2026)
